issue.title: fix: show Blossom thumbnails as posters on video cards
issue.body:
## Summary

#139 changed video preload from `"auto"` to `"none"` to stop the 50-parallel video fetch storm on dashboard render. Side effect: the regular `createVideoCard()` had no `poster` attribute and was relying on `preload="auto"` to decode and display a first frame — without that, cards now show black boxes until you hover.

Add `poster="https://media.divine.video/{sha}.jpg"`. Blossom auto-generates thumbnails keyed by the video sha (verified: HTTP 200 with real JPEG bytes for SAFE videos). For external Blossom imports the URL 404s and the poster simply doesn't render — graceful degradation, no console errors.

This restores the visual moderation experience without re-introducing the video preload storm.

## Test plan

- [ ] Reload `/admin/dashboard?action=REVIEW` — cards now show thumbnails for divine-uploaded videos
- [ ] Network tab: `GET media.divine.video/{sha}.jpg` per card (cheap, cached at edge), still zero `/admin/video/*.mp4` until hover
- [ ] Hover a card — video plays as before
- [ ] External-Blossom imports (REVIEW) without a divine thumbnail show black boxes (acceptable — those videos can't be played either)

issue.title: fix(admin-video): per-fetch try/catch + KV-cache nostr fallback
issue.body:
## Summary

Defense-in-depth on top of #138 + #139, plus a GCS direct fallback.

**Two layers added to `/admin/video/{sha}.mp4` proxy:**

1. **GCS direct fallback** — between stored-`content_url` and the relay-imeta fallback, hit `https://storage.googleapis.com/divine-blossom-media/{sha}` directly. The Blossom CDN sits in front of this bucket and the bucket is publicly readable, so when the CDN returns 404 (moderation enforcement, VCL gates, etc.) the underlying bytes are still reachable without auth or a relay roundtrip. Bucket name configurable via `env.GCS_BUCKET`. CSAM-handled-upstream-at-GCS still applies — these are the same bytes Blossom would have served.

2. **KV-cache the Nostr imeta-url fallback** — the fallback added in #138 opened a fresh WebSocket to relay.divine.video on every miss. With a 50-card dashboard render hitting the proxy in parallel, that meant up to 50 concurrent WS connections per page load — exhausting per-isolate budgets and surfacing as 500/502. Cache the relay lookup result in MODERATION_KV with a 5-min TTL; sentinel empty string represents "no event found" so negative results are also cached. Write goes through `ctx.waitUntil`.

This commit also tightens per-fetch error handling on the upstream chain (CDN, transcode, admin bypass) so a single network hiccup can't 500 the whole request when later fallbacks are exactly designed to cover for it.

**New proxy chain order:**
1. `media.divine.video/{sha}` (CDN, unauthenticated)
2. `media.divine.video/{sha}/720p.mp4` (transcoded MP4 if CDN returned non-playable)
3. `/admin/api/blob/{sha}/content` (admin bypass with secret)
4. Stored `content_url` candidates
5. **NEW:** `storage.googleapis.com/divine-blossom-media/{sha}` (GCS direct)
6. Nostr `imeta` URL via relay (KV-cached)
7. 404

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test -- src/index.test.mjs` (136/136 pass)
- [ ] Deploy and confirm the 500/502 spam in moderator console clears
- [ ] `wrangler tail` shows `[ADMIN] Serving video from gcs-direct` for previously-404ing native videos
- [ ] `wrangler tail` shows `[ADMIN] Serving video from nostr-imeta-url` for external Blossom videos (Plebs, etc.) on cache miss

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

comment.body:
<!-- divine-brain:pr-classifier:real-bug -->
**[real-bug]** This diff adds critical error handling to the admin video proxy endpoint. However, there is a **real bug in the nostr imeta lookup logic**: the code now caches `imetaUrl` (including `null` values as empty strings), but the follow-up validation `if (imetaUrl && imetaUrl !== cdnUrl && imetaUrl !== adminBypassUrl)` runs outside the try/catch block that populates it. If the cache hit returns `null` (encoded as `''`), `imetaUrl` remains `null`, but if the relay lookup throws, the catch block only logs a warning without setting `imetaUrl` — leaving it uninitialized and causing the fallback fetch to be skipped entirely when it shouldn't be. The variable scoping and error path are broken: either initialize `imetaUrl = null` at the top level before the try block, or refactor the logic so the fetch attempt happens inside the protected scope.

<details><summary>signals</summary>

- 
  - "let imetaUrl = null" is declared inside a try block, making it potentially undefined in the outer scope
  - The follow-up check "if (imetaUrl && ...)" at line 2882 runs *after* the try/catch, but imetaUrl may not be bound if the catch branch executes
  - If the relay lookup throws and we catch it, imetaUrl is never assigned, yet the code proceeds to check it outside the try block
  - The cache write and imeta fetch have been separated from their declaration scope, breaking the control flow

</details>

_— divine-brain pr-classifier_

issue.title: feat: report-only review (no pre-moderation of uploads)
issue.body:
## Summary

Stops pre-moderating every upload. Content is playable by default; the team queue surfaces ONLY items a user has reported. Major policy shift agreed with @rabble during the 2026-05-04/05 cost-cut session — keeps T&S queue load proportional to report volume instead of upload volume.

## What changes

| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/scan` | enqueues moderation | `{queued: false, reason: 'reactive_moderation'}` |
| `POST /api/v1/batch-scan` | enqueues each video | per-item `status: 'reactive'` |
| Relay polling cron | enqueues new kind:34236 events | logs observation, does not enqueue |
| `POST /api/v1/report` (NSFW types) | queued for manual-review | writes `action: AGE_RESTRICTED, provider: 'user-report'` row directly |
| `POST /api/v1/report` (other types) | queued for manual-review | writes `action: REVIEW, provider: 'user-report'` row directly |
| `POST /api/v1/report` (AI types) | queued with `forceAIDetection: true` | writes REVIEW row + still records ai_detection_event for telemetry |

NSFW report types matched: `nudity, porn, pornography, nsfw, sexual, sexual_content, explicit, adult, adult_content` (case- and underscore-insensitive). Helper: `isNsfwReportType` in `src/reports.mjs`.

## Why this works

Dashboard's existing `FLAGGED` filter (`src/index.mjs:1488`) already queries `action IN ('REVIEW', 'AGE_RESTRICTED', 'PERMANENT_BAN') AND reviewed_by IS NULL` — both report-driven action types land there automatically. No dashboard change needed.

For absent-row sha256s (the new default for unreported uploads), `/check-result/{sha}` (`src/index.mjs:3890-3900`) returns `status: 'unknown', moderated: false, blocked: false, age_restricted: false` — clients treat as playable.

## Conflict resolution on existing rows

`ON CONFLICT(sha256) DO UPDATE` preserves PERMANENT_BAN, only allows upgrades:
- `SAFE → REVIEW` allowed
- `SAFE/REVIEW → AGE_RESTRICTED` allowed
- Anything else → no change

So a moderator's prior decision (e.g., REVIEW with a reviewed_by) is not clobbered by a subsequent NSFW report.

## Tests

- 804/804 pass (run as `npx vitest run src/index.test.mjs src/reports.test.mjs`)
- New helper unit tests: `isNsfwReportType` matches expected labels case-insensitively
- New endpoint tests: NSFW report writes AGE_RESTRICTED row; non-NSFW report writes REVIEW row; scan + batch-scan + AI-report all assert the queue is NOT touched
- Existing AI-detection telemetry assertions preserved

## Cost shape

| Layer | Before today's session | After PR #131 | After this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hive billing | ~$6k/day | ~zero | ~zero (unchanged) |
| T&S queue load | flagged-by-Hive uploads | every upload | reported items only |

## Risk callouts (T&S team needs to know)

1. **No automated NSFW/violence/hate pre-screen anymore.** Anything legal-but-bad lands publicly until a user reports it. (CSAM remains scanned upstream at GCS via Google hash-matching — unchanged by this PR.)
2. **First report = team sees it** — there is no count threshold anymore. Spam-report potential exists; existing `user_reports` UNIQUE(sha256, reporter_pubkey) prevents the same pubkey from re-reporting.
3. **Existing REVIEW backlog** is left untouched — moderators drain it; new uploads stop adding to it.
4. **PR #132 plumbing** (`forceProvider`, `applyForceProvider`) is left in place but unused. Dead code, harmless. Can be removed later or repurposed if Hive returns.

## Deploys via auto-CI

Auto-deploy via `cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3` on push to main (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:78`). After merge, post-deploy verification:
1. POST a test report with `report_type: 'nudity'` → assert new `action: AGE_RESTRICTED, provider: 'user-report'` row in `moderation_results`
2. POST a test report with `report_type: 'violence'` → assert new `action: REVIEW, provider: 'user-report'` row
3. Confirm `wrangler tail` shows zero queue activity for new Blossom uploads

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Pushed `b136d16` addressing the code review:

- **C1** — `ON CONFLICT` now early-outs on `reviewed_by IS NOT NULL` for action/provider/categories/moderated_at. Moderator decisions are immutable to subsequent reports.
- **I1** — `/api/v1/report` validates with `isValidSha256` + `isValidPubkey`, normalizes sha256 to lowercase, returns 400 on malformed input.
- **I2** — NSFW reports now need 2 distinct `reporter_pubkey`s before auto AGE_RESTRICTED. First NSFW report writes REVIEW. Defends against single-token grief without dropping the user's "auto age-restrict NSFW" intent. (Full hardening would need NIP-98 sig — deferred.)

Tests: 807/807 pass on changed files. New regression tests: malformed sha rejection, malformed pubkey rejection, first-NSFW = REVIEW, NSFW = AGE_RESTRICTED only at count >= 2.

issue.title: fix: moderation team bunker rejects nip44_decrypt — web inbox empty
issue.body:
## Symptom

Members of the support / moderation team logged into the moderation account on `divine.video` see an empty Direct Messages inbox ("No other messages yet"), while the same account has multiple active conversations visible on `moderation.admin.divine.video`.

## Evidence

A direct relay probe of `wss://relay.divine.video` and `wss://nos.lol` against the moderator pubkey shows 14 and 13 distinct `kind:1059` gift wraps respectively in the last 3 days, with the newest 5 event IDs identical across both relays — the events are on the wire and propagating cleanly. The web client receives them but cannot decrypt them.

The web client decrypts via the NIP-46 bunker (Keycast). The admin panel at `moderation.admin.divine.video` decrypts with the raw `NOSTR_PRIVATE_KEY` Cloudflare secret, bypassing Keycast — that's why the admin panel shows messages while the web client doesn't.

## Likely cause

The Keycast team-feature OAuth scopes for moderation-team members do not grant `nip44_decrypt`. `sign_event` and `nip44_encrypt` are likely granted (historic moderation auto-DMs work via `dm-sender.mjs` server-side with the raw key, and manual sends from web have been observed to leave wraps on relays — encrypt path works). The decrypt RPC then rejects every `unwrapDmGiftWrap` call from the web client and the inbox renders empty.

## Recommended fix

Update the Keycast team policy for the moderation team auth to grant `nip44_decrypt` (and `nip04_decrypt` if used). Members will need to reconnect their bunker session afterwards to pick up the new scope.

## Related codebase work (visibility / prevention; does not fix the underlying capability)

Three PRs in `divinevideo/divine-web` make the failure mode loud instead of silent so future regressions don't manifest as a silently empty inbox:

- `divinevideo/divine-web#312` — surface decrypt failures in the inbox UI (closes `divinevideo/divine-web#309`)
- `divinevideo/divine-web#314` — healthcheck NIP-44 capability at signer attach (closes `divinevideo/divine-web#311`)
- `divinevideo/divine-web#313` — make NIP-17 self-wrap non-fatal (closes `divinevideo/divine-web#310`)

After these merge, the user-visible behavior changes from "silently empty inbox" to "inbox temporarily unavailable, signer needs reconnection". **But until the Keycast policy is updated, the moderation team still cannot read DMs from the web client.** That capability fix is this issue.

## Original report

`divinevideo/divine-web#307` — Moderation account messages not showing on moderation page or web.

issue.title: Scale classic Vine rollback relay lookups for large batches
issue.body:
The classic Vine rollback path still resolves Nostr context one SHA at a time for raw SHA-only input.

That is acceptable for small operator runs, but for large incident batches it means many sequential WebSocket connections to the relay and slower rollback execution.

Scope:
- add bounded concurrency or otherwise batch-friendly relay metadata resolution for rollback candidates
- consider preferring pre-resolved `videos` input for large runs
- document safe operator batch sizes if the implementation remains sequential

This is an operational scalability follow-up. The rollback correctness issues were fixed directly in PR #63.

issue.title: Add transcript reprocess retry test for transcript fetch failures
issue.body:
## Problem
The transcript reprocess path catches transcript fetch errors, logs them, and continues, but there is no regression test proving the row stays pending for a later retry when the fetch fails due to network or upstream errors.

## Why this matters
- This path is intentionally best-effort and should remain retryable.
- A small regression could accidentally clear or mutate pending state on transient failures without an obvious test failure.

## Proposed direction
Add an integration-style scheduled-cron test that simulates a thrown fetch or non-202/non-404 fetch failure and asserts that:
- the row remains `transcript_pending = 1`
- it remains eligible for the next cron tick
- no downstream notification is emitted

## Notes
This is follow-up work from PR #107. The PR itself should still fix the migration numbering and manual-moderation overwrite race before merge.

issue.title: Confirm downstream dedupe behavior for repeated moderation label writes after transcript reprocess
issue.body:
## Problem
When transcript reprocess changes the action, the code calls the normal downstream notification path again, including `writeModerationLabels`.

## Why this matters
- If the downstream storage layer does not dedupe repeated writes for the same content/action transition, transcript reprocess can create duplicate label rows.
- This may be acceptable, but it should be verified explicitly rather than assumed.

## Proposed direction
Confirm whether the ClickHouse moderation label path dedupes repeated writes for the same sha/action context. If not, decide whether dedupe belongs in the writer, the schema, or the transcript reprocess caller.

## Notes
This is follow-up work from PR #107. The PR itself should still fix the migration numbering and manual-moderation overwrite race before merge.

issue.title: Recompute or explicitly preserve categories during transcript reprocess
issue.body:
## Problem
Transcript reprocess can change the stored moderation action and scores, but the current implementation writes `categories` back using the pre-existing stored value.

## Why this matters
- The row can end up internally inconsistent: action and scores reflect transcript-aware reclassification while `categories` still reflect the initial run.
- Admin/debug surfaces that rely on stored categories can become misleading.

## Proposed direction
Choose one of these explicitly:
- recompute and persist categories from the reprocessed classification, or
- preserve the existing categories intentionally and document why that is the correct behavior.

## Notes
This is follow-up work from PR #107. The PR itself should still fix the migration numbering and manual-moderation overwrite race before merge.

issue.title: Add abandonment policy for stuck transcript-pending moderation rows
issue.body:
## Problem
Rows marked `transcript_pending = 1` are re-polled on every transcript reprocess cron tick. If Blossom keeps returning `202 Accepted` indefinitely for a given VTT, that row never resolves and remains in the poll set forever.

## Why this matters
- Creates unbounded retry churn for permanently stuck transcripts
- Grows the set of pending rows over time
- Makes cron work less predictable as old stuck rows accumulate

## Proposed direction
Add a max-age / abandonment policy for transcript-pending rows, for example:
- mark as resolved/abandoned after a fixed window such as 7 days
- record an explicit terminal reason in D1/KV
- stop re-polling rows once they cross that threshold

## Notes
This is follow-up work from PR #107. The immediate blocker items for that PR should still be fixed in the PR itself.

issue.title: Warn when transcript reprocess normalizes an unknown moderation action to SAFE
issue.body:
## Problem
`normalizeModerationAction` currently coerces unknown or malformed stored actions to `SAFE` without logging.

## Why this matters
- Hides data-quality problems in D1 rows
- Makes debugging harder if a corrupted or unexpected action appears in production
- Risks masking a real issue by silently falling back to the least severe action

## Proposed direction
Keep the normalization behavior if desired, but emit a warning with the original value and sha so bad data is visible in logs and can be investigated.

## Notes
This is follow-up work from PR #107. The PR itself should still fix the migration numbering and manual-moderation overwrite race before merge.

issue.title: Scale classic Vine rollback relay lookups for large batches
issue.body:
The classic Vine rollback path still resolves Nostr context one SHA at a time for raw SHA-only input.

That is acceptable for small operator runs, but for large incident batches it means many sequential WebSocket connections to the relay and slower rollback execution.

Scope:
- add bounded concurrency or otherwise batch-friendly relay metadata resolution for rollback candidates
- consider preferring pre-resolved `videos` input for large runs
- document safe operator batch sizes if the implementation remains sequential

This is an operational scalability follow-up. The rollback correctness issues were fixed directly in PR #63.

issue.title: Add transcript reprocess retry test for transcript fetch failures
issue.body:
## Problem
The transcript reprocess path catches transcript fetch errors, logs them, and continues, but there is no regression test proving the row stays pending for a later retry when the fetch fails due to network or upstream errors.

## Why this matters
- This path is intentionally best-effort and should remain retryable.
- A small regression could accidentally clear or mutate pending state on transient failures without an obvious test failure.

## Proposed direction
Add an integration-style scheduled-cron test that simulates a thrown fetch or non-202/non-404 fetch failure and asserts that:
- the row remains `transcript_pending = 1`
- it remains eligible for the next cron tick
- no downstream notification is emitted

## Notes
This is follow-up work from PR #107. The PR itself should still fix the migration numbering and manual-moderation overwrite race before merge.
